On November 16, 2026, between 09:30 and 15:55 UTC, some pull request merges on GitHub timed out. On average, 2.9% of merge attempts timed out, with a peak of 7.1% at 15:17 UTC. Some GitHub Actions workflow runs triggered by pull requests were also delayed. Git operations such as push and fetch stayed available, with higher latency. This was a repeat of a shorter event on November 13, between 13:15 and 17:50 UTC, when 1.7% of merges timed out.

Both events had the same cause: some of the storage servers that hold Git repository data reached their disk read bandwidth limits. A merge must be written to every copy of a repository, so one overloaded server slowed merges for every repository it hosts. Read load on these servers had been growing as part of a planned move of repositories to new infrastructure. A disk configuration setting on those servers also made them read far more data than necessary, which cut their usable bandwidth roughly in half. We mitigated the incident by correcting that setting and moving some load away from the busiest servers.

The corrected setting is now applied permanently across our storage fleet. We are adding storage capacity in the affected region and alerting on per-server disk bandwidth so we catch saturation before it affects customers. Sustained merge timeouts will now page our on-call engineers directly. We are also adding capacity checks before moving repositories or traffic onto new infrastructure.

title: Degraded Availability for MAI Code 2 Flash in Copilot

updates.body: We are investigating reports of degraded performance for Copilot AI Model Providers

We are experiencing degraded availability for the MAI Code 2 Flash model in Copilot products and IDE surfaces. This is due to an issue with an upstream model provider. While we work with them to resolve the issue, we recommend choosing another model or selecting ‘Copilot Fusion’ to continue using Copilot.

We have been working with the upstream provider and applying mitigations, and are seeing widespread improvement in availability for MAI Code 2 Flash across Copilot products and IDE surfaces.
We will continue monitoring.
The degradation affecting Copilot AI Model Providers has been mitigated. We are monitoring to ensure stability.

The issues with our upstream model provider have been resolved, and MAI Code 2 Flash is once again available in Copilot products and IDE surfaces.
We will continue monitoring to ensure stability, but mitigation is complete.
This incident has been resolved. Thank you for your patience and understanding as we addressed this issue. A detailed root cause analysis will be shared as soon as it is available.

updates.body: We are investigating reports of impacted performance for some GitHub services.

Starting around 18:02 UTC on November 5, GitHub web sessions stopped being renewed based on recent activity, so users were signed out when their sessions expired due to inactivity. These sign-outs were caused by a bug in session renewal, not due to a security incident.

We believe we fixed the bug at 05:23 UTC on November 19, and sessions created since then should renew as usual. We’re continuing to monitor the situation.

If you had an inactive session from that period, you may still find that you’re signed out when you return to GitHub. If that happens, all you need to do is sign back in.
The degradation has been mitigated. We are monitoring to ensure stability.

Between November 5, 2026, at 18:02 UTC and November 19, 2026, at 18:05 UTC, GitHub users experienced unexpected expiration of their web browser sessions despite continued activity, requiring them to login. An authentication change introduced an issue that caused web requests to bypass the session activity updates and cookie renewal that normally extend session lifetime. Affected sessions consequently expired when they reached their initial expiration time.

We mitigated the incident by deploying a fix to ensure that continued web activity renews session expiration and browser cookies.

We are adding monitoring to detect unexpected drops in session renewal activity, helping us catch similar issues sooner and reduce their impact on users.
